steps.text: Slice the top off of each tomato. Hollow out each tomato with a spoon, leaving a 1/2 to 1/4 inch shell. Place tomato pulp in a large bowl.

Stir the vinegar and olive oil into the pulp, mixing to break up any large pieces. Season with salt and pepper. Evenly spoon the filling into the tomato shells. Refrigerate for at least 10 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Deviled Tomatoes
raw_recipe.description: Tomatoes are hollowed out and the pulp is mixed with a simple vinaigrette. Serve as a light first course or a super side dish for grilled meat or fish.
raw_recipe.name: Deviled Tomatoes

review.reviewBody: Thank you so much for this concept! I had some extra roma tomatoes to use up and used those. I made some revisions though and used balsamic vinegar instead of distilled white and I added some basil, panko bread crumbs and shredded mozzarella to the filling plus one small roma diced. I topped it off with some parmesan and baked for 10 minutes at 350. They were delicious! Thank you for providing the jumping off point for a spontaneous side dish!

After reading the reviews I decided to try something odd. Made one tomato with regular vinegar, one with red wine vinegar, and one with balsamic vinegar. I added about a teaspoon of onion to each mixture as well as a tiny bit of cheese. The outcome was if you want something super tangy and powerful go with regular vinegar. More of a mild flavor definitely the red wine vinegar. If you are looking for something that will remind you more of like bruschetta then the balsamic. All are great though the regular vinegar made my lips pucker lol. Never had such a sour tomato, but interestingly good.

I had a little trouble scooping out the pulp of my tomatoes so I chopped them up added the other ingredients and made a salad. The inly change I made was to add garlic and a little sugar to cut the acid in the tomatoes since they can give me indigestion.

These were fun to make and very good! I used some smaller tomatoes that I had in the garden. Also I added in some onion, fresh basil, garlic powder and used red wine vinegar. This reminded me of the tomato salads that we make all summer long, but with a cute spin by using the whole, hollowed out tomato. I think these would be wonderful w/ any salad additions that you like. Thank You for sharing this wonderful idea! :)
